_comment: COUPLING tier-2. 'the best theta is theta ~ 1/(1+rho) ... swept over rho from 1/4 to 9, the fastest constant theta was 1/(1+rho) at EVERY ratio' — the single number the knowledge tells an agent to compute before running anything. An optimal claim cannot be checked by running the optimum; it needs neighbours, and neighbours that are themselves STABLE, or the comparison is against thetas that diverge and proves only the stability limit that theta_stability_limit already covers. So the bracket is multiplicative and rho-independent — 0.6x, 1.0x and 1.4x of 1/(1+rho), every one below the limit 2/(1+rho) at every rho by construction — and the contest is between three converging choices. Each run's physics is checked against the closed form as well, because a theta that reached the tolerance fastest by settling on the wrong fixed point would otherwise win.
